newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft on pre-weekend swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft on pre-weekend swaps.

text.p: Mexico's 48- and 24-hour peso contracts closed weak Friday on swaps ahead of the weekend in a session where volume was low due to lack of foreign dealers, traders said.

"I haven't seen many foreigners, they don't want to step in for now, and that made the session boring," said a peso trader. "The peso weakened before the close on demand for dollars from those who had yet to cover positions."
Interbank 24-hour and 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.1 and 1.9 centavos softer, respectively, at 7.5400/7.5440 and 7.5330/7.5390 per dollar.

Dealers often swap same-day for 24-hour or 48-hour dollar contracts prior to a weekend. The advantage is that longer contracts need not be paid for until after the weekend, using pesos that can meanwhile be invested in the money market.
The same-day peso earlier closed 0.2 of a centavo firmer at 7.5210/7.5255 per dollar.
Traders said dealing by foreign investors was dulled by the approaching close of the fiscal year.

"Even though U.S. long-bond rates have fallen, foreigners have stepped out of peso investments," said a peso trader, referring to the 30-year Treasury bond rate which stood at 6.91 percent when the peso market closed.
Traders said that the dollar might be in demand and thus weaken the peso next week as domestic primary rates might fall again.
